Topics · Death and what comes after

What is weighed on the Day of Judgment?

A just scale for deeds, each soul answering for its own, no atom of good lost, and God's mercy open beside it.

Part 1 of 4

﴿فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ٦ فَهُوَ فِى عِيشَةٍ رَّاضِيَةٍ٧ وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَٰزِينُهُۥ٨ فَأُمُّهُۥ هَاوِيَةٌ٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

Then as for one whose scales are heavy [with good deeds], He will be in a pleasant life. But as for one whose scales are light, His refuge[1977] will be an abyss.[1978]

Translator's notes

[1977] Literally, "mother" (a man's original refuge) , which will envelop him as in an embrace. [1978] i.e., the pit of Hellfire.

Quran · Al-Qari'ah 101:6-9

Translation

(let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);

Original · Hebrew

יִשְׁקְלֵ֥נִי בְמֹאזְנֵי־צֶ֑דֶק וְיֵדַ֥ע אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ תֻּמָּתִֽי׃

Job · 31:6

World English Bible

﴿قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins.[1354] Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

Translator's notes

[1354] For those who repent and correct themselves.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:53

Translation

Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to Yahweh, and he will have mercy on him, to our God, for he will freely pardon.

Original · Hebrew

יַעֲזֹ֤ב רָשָׁע֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אָ֖וֶן מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֑יו וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וִֽירַחֲמֵ֔הוּ וְאֶל־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ כִּֽי־יַרְבֶּ֥ה לִסְלֽוֹחַ׃

Isaiah · 55:7

World English Bible

If what we do means anything, it has to carry weight. These verses describe scales that are heavy for some and light for others, and they tie what comes next to what is on them. So the matter is what a person brought, more than who a person was. The verse beside them keeps hope standing: one who went too far is told not to despair. The scale and the mercy belong to one scene.

A question for you

What do people usually expect to count in their favour?

If you sayFamily name or belonging.
ThenKeep that answer. A later part sets it before the verses.
If you sayWhat I believe.
ThenFaith has its place in all this, and the last part shows it joined to deeds.
If you sayWhat I have done.
ThenThat is what the scales speak of, with mercy beside them.

﴿وَنَضَعُ ٱلْمَوَٰزِينَ ٱلْقِسْطَ لِيَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَـٰمَةِ فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْـًٔا ۖ وَإِن كَانَ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا ۗ وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَـٰسِبِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:53

Translation

Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness. According to the multitude of your tender mercies, blot out my transgressions. Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity. Cleanse me from my sin.

Original · Hebrew

חָנֵּ֣נִי אֱלֹהִ֣ים כְּחַסְדֶּ֑ךָ כְּרֹ֥ב רַ֝חֲמֶ֗יךָ מְחֵ֣ה פְשָׁעָֽי׃ הֶ֭רֶב כַּבְּסֵ֣נִי מֵעֲוֺנִ֑י וּֽמֵחַטָּאתִ֥י טַהֲרֵֽנִי׃

the Psalms · 51:1-2

World English Bible

A scale is just only if it leaves nothing out. The verse describes scales of justice on which no soul is treated unfairly in the least, and a deed the weight of a mustard seed is brought forward. Exactness here is good news. Every small kindness you thought was lost is kept, and no one will carry what they did not do.

A question for you

What do you find in exactness like this?

If you sayComfort.
ThenThen you are reading it as a promise: no good is lost.
If you sayHeaviness.
ThenMany feel that, which is why this verse is not read alone. Look at 39:53 beside it.
If you sayI doubt anything like this is possible.
ThenThen the question is whether a reckoning makes sense at all, and that has its own Step.

Translation of the meaning

It [i.e., Paradise] is not [obtained] by your wishful thinking nor by that of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does a wrong will be recompensed for it, and he will not find besides Allāh a protector or a helper. And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer - those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:123-124

Translation

“I, Yahweh, search the mind. I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.”

Original · Hebrew

אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה חֹקֵ֥ר לֵ֖ב בֹּחֵ֣ן כְּלָי֑וֹת וְלָתֵ֤ת לְאִישׁ֙ כִּדְרָכָ֔יו כִּפְרִ֖י מַעֲלָלָֽיו׃

Jeremiah · 17:10

World English Bible

If belonging were enough, those who did good and those who did not would be equal under one banner, and that would not be justice. The first passage says no one carries another's load, and a person has what they strove for. The second sets wishful claims aside: yours and those of others. It addresses everyone, and Muslims first. Each is asked about what they did.

A question for you

Which of these claims is closest to your own people?

If you sayWe are the people of the true religion.
Then4:123 speaks to every party on this, and first to those who believe in it.
If you sayWe come from a noble family.
ThenThere is a whole question on this, including descent from the Prophet himself.
If you sayI belong to no group.
ThenThen the verses ask you one thing: what has your striving carried?

who forgives all your sins, who heals all your diseases, who redeems your life from destruction, who crowns you with loving kindness and tender mercies, who satisfies your desire with good things, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle’s.

Original · Hebrew

הַסֹּלֵ֥חַ לְכָל־עֲוֺנֵ֑כִי הָ֝רֹפֵ֗א לְכָל־תַּחֲלֻאָֽיְכִי׃ הַגּוֹאֵ֣ל מִשַּׁ֣חַת חַיָּ֑יְכִי הַֽ֝מְעַטְּרֵ֗כִי חֶ֣סֶד וְרַחֲמִֽים׃ הַמַּשְׂבִּ֣יַע בַּטּ֣וֹב עֶדְיֵ֑ךְ תִּתְחַדֵּ֖שׁ כַּנֶּ֣שֶׁר נְעוּרָֽיְכִי׃

the Psalms · 103:3-5

World English Bible

If deeds are what is weighed, where do faith and mercy stand? The verse joins them: whoever hopes to meet their Lord, let them do good, and give no one a share in His worship. Faith is the root and direction of the deed, and the deed is faith's honesty. The second verse says mercy reaches those who fell short. The picture is three things together, and none stands without the others.

A question for you

How would you describe the relation between the three?

If you sayFaith directs the deed.
ThenThat follows the order of 18:110. The question of deeds without faith remains.
If you sayMercy exceeds everything.
ThenMercy is wide. Why work, then? That question has its own Step.
If you sayThe deed is the proof.
ThenThe verses grant that, and add that one who fell finds mercy waiting.
